title: Proactive DR validation and live-swap procedures for active-passive regions
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Create and validate a repeatable, low-risk active->passive region live-swap procedure that tests backup/restore integrity, SLO preservation, circuit-breaker behavior, and automated load-shedding. This ticket covers authoring the runbook steps, automating critical validation checks, expanding monitoring/alerts to detect regressions, and scheduling quarterly live-swap drills with staged rollbacks.
background_and_rationale: We have observed that passive-region drills executed as isolated restore tests do not adequately exercise the full live-swap surface: global DNS updates, cross-region caches (KV cache priming), circuit-breaker propagation, downstream async queues, and cost-aware load-shedding. Recent incidents (see postmortem INF-2025-11) showed slow detection of degraded tail latency after a region swap. This initiative enforces a holistic validation flow to reduce recovery time and prevent SLO regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Author a step-by-step live-swap runbook that can be executed by oncall + infra engineer in <= 90 minutes (excluding data restore time)
Automated pre-checks that verify backup integrity (checksum, manifest) and restore success against a verification cluster
Circuit breaker thresholds documented and testable: open/harden at simulated overload and recover automatically
Load-shedding policy exercised with synthetic traffic to demonstrate graceful degradation while preserving critical SLOs
Observability: SLO dashboard shows expected metrics during and after swap (error budget burn, p95/p99 latency, token throughput)
Post-drill report template that contains lessons learned, regression diffs, and remediation tasks
Schedule: First full live-swap drill run end-to-end with a canary traffic slice (5% traffic) followed by full swap in <= 60 days from ticket close
runbook_steps: Pre-drill: Announce window to stakeholders (oncall, CS, Sales) and tag active customer groups to exclude high-risk tenants
Pre-drill: Run automated backup verification job for primary region and confirm manifest+checksums within 1 hour
Step 1: Provision verification cluster in passive region using same runtime-1.22 config and deploy model artifacts via verified restore
Step 2: Execute KV cache priming script with representative prompt set to populate common prefixes
Step 3: Deploy updated circuit-breaker rules in passive region (testing mode) and validate open/close via synthetic overload
Step 4: Shift 5% of production traffic using traffic router (smart-routing policy) to passive region and monitor SLO dashboard for 15 minutes
Step 5: If SLOs stable, increment to 25% for additional 20 minutes; otherwise trigger rollback criteria
Step 6: When confident, perform full traffic cutover and enable global load-shedding policy tuned for passive capacity
Step 7: During swap, verify async queue consumers start against passive endpoints and no message loss occurs (consumer offsets, DLQ counts)
Step 8: Run dedicated backup/restore smoke tests post-cutover (sample queries and embedding reconciliation)
Step 9: After steady-state 60 minutes, execute swapback to primary to validate swap reversal and cleanup
Step 10: Close drill, upload artifacts (metrics, logs, audit trail) and create post-drill report with action items
rollback_criteria_and_signal_checks: p99 read or generation latency > 2x SLO baseline for > 5 minutes
error rate (5xx) increase > 0.5% absolute for > 3 minutes
consumer lag growth > 2x baseline for critical queues
data restore checksum mismatch or missing artifact detection
automation failure in DNS propagation or traffic router that leaves > 10% clients misrouted
test_matrix: Backup validation: checksum verification, manifest integrity, partial-restore validation (first 1M keys)
Circuit breaker test: simulate token spike to exercise open/half-open behavior and confirm failover to compatible model tier
Load-shedding: synthetic traffic mix (80% gen, 15% embeddings, 5% rerank) to validate graceful degradation policies
KV cache priming: cold-start vs warmed performance comparison and hit-rate targets
End-to-end functional checks: sample prompts and structured output validation (function-calling paths)
Security checks: KMS access, IAM role mapping, and audit log continuity post-restore
observability_and_dashboards: SLO dashboard (runtime-slo-view) with p50/p95/p99 latency and token throughput by region
Failover health view showing region IPs, routing state, and recent DNS TTL changes
Circuit-breaker map showing per-route status and recent openings
Backup/restore verification dashboard with manifest age, checksum results, and restore duration histograms
Drill-run dashboard: synthetic traffic slice, queue lag, and error budget burn rate
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: DNS propagation delays causing partial client routing inconsistencies. Mitigation: Use traffic router with per-client sticky routing and health checks; pre-warm DNS with low TTL and staged cutover.
Risk: KV cache cold-start causes spike in latency. Mitigation: Run priming job with representative prompt set; keep small warmers for critical prefixes.
Risk: Circuit-breaker misconfiguration causes unnecessary open states. Mitigation: Test circuit-breaker rules in canary mode and include automatic revert-on-failure.
Risk: Restore performance exceeds time budget. Mitigation: Validate restore times in a dry-run window and parallelize artifact pulls when possible.
